status_detail: Local report says City of Iola sold 10 acres north of Russell Stover Chocolates to Vine Energy LLC in August 2025 for a planned 3 MW data center on Marshmallow Lane; equipment was expected in late 2025 and DCD reported in June 2026 that groundwork had begun with the facility due live by September 2026.
notes: Iola is the Allen County seat. Local source provides primary project facts: 10-acre city land sale, Vine Energy LLC of Overland Park, 3 MW load, 60x60-foot building, option for another 10 acres. No county-level official data-center page found on allencounty.org during targeted search.

status_detail: Barber County hosts an official data-center document page and project website. Project materials identify Project Helium in Barber County, Kansas; Google materials describe a potential air-cooled campus of up to 3 data center buildings plus support buildings, early earthwork targeted for early 2027 and operations by 2030. A tax/PILOT projection document says two data center buildings were scheduled for completion in 2029 and 2030, respectively, with incentives requested per phase.
notes: Official materials also cite 300+ jobs on the public project site, while a January 2026 Google deck says up to 500 FTE at full buildout; capacity was not disclosed in official sources reviewed. Location is near Sharon / Lone Tree Road area based on project naming and county materials.

status_detail: No Brown County data center project found. Brown County official zoning materials show policy activity: a 2026 moratorium/resolution category for data centers/BESS/chip manufacturing and an August 5, 2026 public hearing notice to define and prohibit data centers and BESS, but no specific data-center application or developer was identified.
notes: Because the county appears to be regulating or prohibiting the use rather than evaluating a named project, this is recorded as no_projects_found rather than a rejected project.

status_detail: City of El Dorado official statement on May 22, 2026 confirmed the city had met with a developer inquiring about the possibility of developing a data center in or near El Dorado, while clarifying that the zoning text amendment under consideration did not approve a specific project and that any zoning, special-use permit, incentives, or infrastructure extension would require open public approval. Butler County has a dedicated data-center document page with draft county CUP/regulation materials in July-August 2026.
notes: Developer and site are not named in official sources. Local/social chatter names Beltline Energy, but that was not confirmed in the official city/county pages reviewed, so developer is left null. The El Dorado Inc. public information site discusses potential data-center development and possible >$1B investment scenarios but says it is not affiliated with a developer or government.
